verses.original: Ὅσοι εἰσὶν ὑπὸ ζυγὸν δοῦλοι τοὺς ἰδίους δεσπότας πάσης τιμῆς ἀξίους ἡγείσθωσαν ἵνα μὴ τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ ἡ διδασκαλία βλασφημῆται
verses.transliteration: Hosoi eisin hypo zygon douloi tous idious despotas pasēs timēs axious hēgeisthōsan hina mē to onoma tou Theou kai hē didaskalia blasphēmētai
verses.literal: All who are under the yoke of slavery should regard their . . . masters as fully worthy of honor so that God’s name and our teaching will not be discredited
verses.literalPt: Todos os servos que estão debaixo do jugo estimem a seus senhores como dignos de toda honra, a fim de que o nome de Deus e a doutrina não sejam blasfemados.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ πιστοὺς ἔχοντες δεσπότας μὴ καταφρονείτωσαν ὅτι ἀδελφοί εἰσιν ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον δουλευέτωσαν ὅτι πιστοί εἰσιν καὶ ἀγαπητοὶ οἱ τῆς εὐεργεσίας ἀντιλαμβανόμενοι Ταῦτα δίδασκε καὶ παρακάλει
verses.transliteration: hoi de pistous echontes despotas mē kataphroneitōsan hoti adelphoi eisin alla mallon douleuetōsan hoti pistoi eisin kai agapētoi hoi tēs euergesias antilambanomenoi Tauta didaske kai parakalei
verses.literal: Those who have believing masters should not show disrespect because they are brothers but should serve them all the more since those receiving their good service are beloved believers Teach and encourage these principles
verses.literalPt: Aqueles que têm senhores crentes não os desprezem, porque são irmãos; antes, os sirvam melhor, porque os que se aproveitam do seu trabalho são crentes e amigos. Ensina e recomenda essas coisas.

verses.original: Εἴ τις ἑτεροδιδασκαλεῖ καὶ μὴ προσέρχεται ὑγιαίνουσιν λόγοις τοῖς τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ τῇ κατ’ εὐσέβειαν διδασκαλίᾳ
verses.transliteration: Ei tis heterodidaskalei kai mē proserchetai hygiainousin logois tois tou Kyriou hēmōn Iēsou Christou kai tē kat’ eusebeian didaskalia
verses.literal: If anyone teaches another doctrine and disagrees with the sound words of our Lord Jesus Christ and with godly teaching
verses.literalPt: Se alguém ensina doutrina diversa e não aceita as sãs palavras de nosso Senhor Jesus Cristo e a doutrina segundo a piedade,

verses.original: τετύφωται μηδὲν ἐπιστάμενος ἀλλὰ νοσῶν περὶ ζητήσεις καὶ λογομαχίας ἐξ ὧν γίνεται φθόνος ἔρις βλασφημίαι ὑπόνοιαι πονηραί
verses.transliteration: tetyphōtai mēden epistamenos alla nosōn peri zētēseis kai logomachias ex hōn ginetai phthonos eris blasphēmiai hyponoiai ponērai
verses.literal: he is conceited and understands nothing Instead he has an unhealthy interest in controversies and disputes about words out of which come envy strife abusive talk evil suspicions
verses.literalPt: este é cheio de orgulho e nada sabe, mas delira acerca de questões e contendas de palavras, das quais se originam invejas, brigas, calúnias, suspeitas injustas

verses.original: διαπαρατριβαὶ διεφθαρμένων ἀνθρώπων τὸν νοῦν καὶ ἀπεστερημένων τῆς ἀληθείας νομιζόντων πορισμὸν εἶναι τὴν εὐσέβειαν
verses.transliteration: diaparatribai diephtharmenōn anthrōpōn ton noun kai apesterēmenōn tēs alētheias nomizontōn porismon einai tēn eusebeian
verses.literal: and constant friction between men of depraved mind who are devoid of the truth These men regard godliness as a means of gain
verses.literalPt: e discussões intermináveis da parte de pessoas perversas de entendimento, privadas da verdade, julgando que a piedade é um mero interesse.

verses.original: Ἔστιν δὲ πορισμὸς μέγας ἡ εὐσέβεια μετὰ αὐταρκείας
verses.transliteration: Estin de porismos megas hē eusebeia meta autarkeias
verses.literal: Of course godliness with contentment is great gain
verses.literalPt: A piedade, com o contentamento, é grande lucro,

verses.original: οὐδὲν γὰρ εἰσηνέγκαμεν εἰς τὸν κόσμον ὅτι οὐδὲ ἐξενεγκεῖν τι δυνάμεθα
verses.transliteration: ouden gar eisēnenkamen eis ton kosmon hoti oude exenenkein ti dynametha
verses.literal: For we brought nothing into the world so we cannot carry anything out of it
verses.literalPt: porque nada trouxemos para este mundo, nem nada podemos levar dele;

verses.original: ἔχοντες δὲ διατροφὰς καὶ σκεπάσματα τούτοις ἀρκεσθησόμεθα
verses.transliteration: echontes de diatrophas kai skepasmata toutois arkesthēsometha
verses.literal: But if we have food and clothing we will be content with these
verses.literalPt: tendo alimento e vestuário, deveremos ficar satisfeitos com isso.

verses.original: Οἱ δὲ βουλόμενοι πλουτεῖν ἐμπίπτουσιν εἰς πειρασμὸν καὶ παγίδα καὶ ἐπιθυμίας πολλὰς ἀνοήτους καὶ βλαβεράς αἵτινες βυθίζουσιν τοὺς ἀνθρώπους εἰς ὄλεθρον καὶ ἀπώλειαν
verses.transliteration: Hoi de boulomenoi ploutein empiptousin eis peirasmon kai pagida kai epithymias pollas anoētous kai blaberas haitines bythizousin tous anthrōpous eis olethron kai apōleian
verses.literal: Those who want to be rich however fall into temptation and become ensnared by many foolish and harmful desires that plunge them into ruin and destruction
verses.literalPt: Os que querem tornar-se ricos caem em tentação, e em laço, e em muitos desejos insensatos e nocivos, os quais arrastam os homens à ruína e à perdição.

verses.original: ῥίζα γὰρ πάντων τῶν κακῶν ἐστιν ἡ φιλαργυρία ἧς τινες ὀρεγόμενοι ἀπεπλανήθησαν ἀπὸ τῆς πίστεως καὶ ἑαυτοὺς περιέπειραν ὀδύναις πολλαῖς
verses.transliteration: rhiza gar pantōn tōn kakōn estin hē philargyria hēs tines oregomenoi apeplanēthēsan apo tēs pisteōs kai heautous periepeiran odynais pollais
verses.literal: For the love of money is the root of all kinds of evil By craving it some have wandered away from the faith and pierced themselves with many sorrows
verses.literalPt: Pois o amor do dinheiro é raiz de todos os males; e alguns, cobiçando-o, se desviaram da fé e se traspassaram a si mesmos com muitas dores.

verses.original: Σὺ δέ ὦ ἄνθρωπε Θεοῦ ταῦτα φεῦγε δίωκε δὲ δικαιοσύνην εὐσέβειαν πίστιν ἀγάπην ὑπομονήν πραϋπαθίαν
verses.transliteration: Sy de ō anthrōpe Theou tauta pheuge diōke de dikaiosynēn eusebeian pistin agapēn hypomonēn praupathian
verses.literal: But you O man of God flee from these things and pursue righteousness godliness faith love perseverance and gentleness
verses.literalPt: Tu, porém, ó homem de Deus, foge dessas coisas; segue a justiça, a piedade, a fé, o amor, a perseverança, a mansidão.

verses.original: ἀγωνίζου τὸν καλὸν ἀγῶνα τῆς πίστεως ἐπιλαβοῦ τῆς αἰωνίου ζωῆς εἰς ἣν ἐκλήθης καὶ ὡμολόγησας τὴν καλὴν ὁμολογίαν ἐνώπιον πολλῶν μαρτύρων
verses.transliteration: agōnizou ton kalon agōna tēs pisteōs epilabou tēs aiōniou zōēs eis hēn eklēthēs kai hōmologēsas tēn kalēn homologian enōpion pollōn martyrōn
verses.literal: Fight the good fight of the faith Take hold of the eternal life to which you were called when you made the good confession before many witnesses
verses.literalPt: Peleja a boa peleja da fé; apodera-te da vida eterna, para a qual foste chamado, tendo feito uma boa confissão diante de muitas testemunhas.

verses.original: Παραγγέλλω σοι ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ ζωογονοῦντος τὰ πάντα καὶ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ μαρτυρήσαντος ἐπὶ Ποντίου Πιλάτου τὴν καλὴν ὁμολογίαν
verses.transliteration: Parangellō soi enōpion tou Theou tou zōogonountos ta panta kai Christou Iēsou tou martyrēsantos epi Pontiou Pilatou tēn kalēn homologian
verses.literal: I charge you in the presence of God who gives life to all things and of Christ Jesus who made the good confession in His testimony before Pontius Pilate
verses.literalPt: Eu te exorto, diante de Deus, que dá vida a todas as coisas, e diante de Jesus Cristo, que perante Pôncio Pilatos fez sua boa confissão,

verses.original: τηρῆσαί σε τὴν ἐντολὴν ἄσπιλον ἀνεπίλημπτον μέχρι τῆς ἐπιφανείας τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ
verses.transliteration: tērēsai se tēn entolēn aspilon anepilēmpton mechri tēs epiphaneias tou Kyriou hēmōn Iēsou Christou
verses.literal: Keep . . . this commandment without stain or reproach until the appearance of our Lord Jesus Christ
verses.literalPt: que guardes este mandamento sem mácula nem repreensão, até a vinda de nosso Senhor Jesus Cristo;

verses.original: ἣν καιροῖς ἰδίοις δείξει ὁ μακάριος καὶ μόνος Δυνάστης ὁ Βασιλεὺς τῶν βασιλευόντων καὶ Κύριος τῶν κυριευόντων
verses.transliteration: hēn kairois idiois deixei ho makarios kai monos Dynastēs ho Basileus tōn basileuontōn kai Kyrios tōn kyrieuontōn
verses.literal: which the blessed and only Sovereign One the King of kings and Lord of lords will bring about in His own time
verses.literalPt: a qual, no tempo próprio, mostrará o bem-aventurado e único Soberano, o Rei dos reis e o Senhor dos senhores,

verses.original: ὁ μόνος ἔχων ἀθανασίαν φῶς οἰκῶν ἀπρόσιτον ὃν εἶδεν οὐδεὶς ἀνθρώπων οὐδὲ ἰδεῖν δύναται ᾧ τιμὴ καὶ κράτος αἰώνιον ἀμήν
verses.transliteration: ho monos echōn athanasian phōs oikōn aprositon hon eiden oudeis anthrōpōn oude idein dynatai hō timē kai kratos aiōnion amēn
verses.literal: He alone is immortal and dwells in unapproachable light No one has ever seen Him nor can anyone see Him To Him be honor and eternal dominion Amen
verses.literalPt: aquele que só possui a imortalidade e que habita em luz inacessível, a quem nenhum dos homens tem visto, nem pode ver; ao qual seja dada honra e poder eterno. Amém.

verses.original: Τοῖς πλουσίοις ἐν τῷ νῦν αἰῶνι παράγγελλε μὴ ὑψηλοφρονεῖν μηδὲ ἠλπικέναι ἐπὶ πλούτου ἀδηλότητι ἀλλ’ ἐπὶ Θεῷ τῷ παρέχοντι ἡμῖν πάντα πλουσίως εἰς ἀπόλαυσιν
verses.transliteration: Tois plousiois en tō nyn aiōni parangelle mē hypsēlophronein mēde ēlpikenai epi ploutou adēlotēti all’ epi Theō tō parechonti hēmin panta plousiōs eis apolausin
verses.literal: Instruct those who are rich in the present age not to be conceited and not to put their hope in the uncertainty of wealth but in God who richly provides all things for us to enjoy
verses.literalPt: Exorta os ricos deste mundo a que não sejam orgulhosos, nem esperem na incerteza das riquezas, mas em Deus, que nos concede abundantemente todas as coisas para delas gozarmos;

verses.original: ἀγαθοεργεῖν πλουτεῖν ἐν ἔργοις καλοῖς εὐμεταδότους εἶναι κοινωνικούς
verses.transliteration: agathoergein ploutein en ergois kalois eumetadotous einai koinōnikous
verses.literal: Instruct them to do good to be rich in good works and to be generous and ready to share
verses.literalPt: que pratiquem o bem, que se enriqueçam de boas obras, que sejam generosos e liberais,

verses.original: ἀποθησαυρίζοντας ἑαυτοῖς θεμέλιον καλὸν εἰς τὸ μέλλον ἵνα ἐπιλάβωνται τῆς ὄντως ζωῆς
verses.transliteration: apothēsaurizontas heautois themelion kalon eis to mellon hina epilabōntai tēs ontōs zōēs
verses.literal: treasuring up for themselves a firm foundation for the future so that they may take hold of that which is truly life
verses.literalPt: entesourando para si um fundamento sólido para o futuro, a fim de que se apoderem da vida que é realmente vida.

verses.original: Ὦ Τιμόθεε τὴν παραθήκην φύλαξον ἐκτρεπόμενος τὰς βεβήλους κενοφωνίας καὶ ἀντιθέσεις τῆς ψευδωνύμου γνώσεως
verses.transliteration: Ō Timothee tēn parathēkēn phylaxon ektrepomenos tas bebēlous kenophōnias kai antitheseis tēs pseudōnymou gnōseōs
verses.literal: O Timothy guard what has been entrusted to you Avoid irreverent empty chatter and the opposing arguments of so-called knowledge
verses.literalPt: Ó Timóteo, guarda o que te foi confiado, evitando as conversas vãs e profanas e as objeções de uma falsa ciência,

verses.original: ἥν τινες ἐπαγγελλόμενοι περὶ τὴν πίστιν ἠστόχησαν Ἡ χάρις μεθ’ ὑμῶν
verses.transliteration: hēn tines epangellomenoi peri tēn pistin ēstochēsan Hē charis meth’ hymōn
verses.literal: which some have professed and thus swerved away from the faith Grace be with you all
verses.literalPt: a qual, tendo alguns professado, se desviaram da fé. A graça seja convosco.
